chapters.chapterDescription: Master the building blocks of digital electronics! Learn how simple gates like AND, OR, and XOR form the foundation of all computer logic. By combining these basic gates, you'll create increasingly powerful circuits that perform complex operations.

levelsV2.name: NOT Gate
levelsV2.description: Output should be the inverse of input.

levelsV2.name: AND Gate
levelsV2.description: Output should be 1 only if both inputs are 1.

levelsV2.name: OR Gate
levelsV2.description: Output should be 1 if either input is 1.

levelsV2.name: XOR Gate
levelsV2.description: Output should be 1 if exactly one input is 1.

levelsV2.name: NOR Gate
levelsV2.description: Output is 1 only when both inputs are 0.

levelsV2.name: XNOR Gate
levelsV2.description: Output is 1 when inputs are equal.

chapters.chapterDescription: Building upon basic logic gates, these challenges introduce more complex combinational circuits, multi-input functions, and fundamental functional blocks. Master the art of combining simple gates to create sophisticated logic operations.

levelsV2.name: A AND NOT B
levelsV2.description: Output should be 1 when A=1 and B=0.

levelsV2.name: A OR NOT B
levelsV2.description: Output should be 1 when A=1 or B=0 (or both).

levelsV2.name: Implication (A → B)
levelsV2.description: (!A) OR B.

levelsV2.name: 3-Input AND
levelsV2.description: Output is 1 only when A=B=C=1.

levelsV2.name: 3-Input OR
levelsV2.description: Output is 1 if any input is 1.

levelsV2.name: Majority
levelsV2.description: Output is 1 when at least two inputs are 1.

levelsV2.name: Parity (Odd, 3-bit)
levelsV2.description: Output is 1 when the number of 1s is odd.

levelsV2.name: At Least One Zero
levelsV2.description: Output is 1 unless both inputs are 1.

levelsV2.name: 2→1 MUX (S,A,B)
levelsV2.description: If S=0 output A; if S=1 output B.

chapters.chapterDescription: Enter the world of memory and time! Build circuits that remember their past and create counters, latches, and flip-flops. This is where digital circuits gain the power of memory and state.

levelsV2.name: SR Latch
levelsV2.description: Basic memory element. Set when S=1, Reset when R=1, Hold when both are 0.

levelsV2.name: D Latch
levelsV2.description: Level-triggered memory element. When Enable=1, Q follows D. When Enable=0, Q holds its value (latched).

levelsV2.name: D Flip-Flop
levelsV2.description: Data storage element. Q follows D on rising clock edge. Q' is the complement of Q. When CLK goes high, Q captures the value of D and holds it until the next rising edge.

chapters.chapterDescription: Learn the magic of binary math! Construct adders from simple gates, understand carry propagation, and build the mathematical foundation that powers every computer's arithmetic unit.

levelsV2.name: Half Adder
levelsV2.description: Add two single bits. Output is sum and carry.

levelsV2.name: 4-bit Adder
levelsV2.description: Add two 4-bit numbers. Output is 5-bit result (4-bit sum + carry).

chapters.chapterDescription: Reach the pinnacle of digital design! Build subtraction circuits using two's complement, create comparators, and finally construct a complete ALU - the heart of every processor that performs all arithmetic and logic operations.

levelsV2.name: 4-bit Subtractor
levelsV2.description: Subtract B from A using two's complement. Output is difference and borrow.

levelsV2.name: 4-bit Comparator
levelsV2.description: Compare two 4-bit numbers. Output A>B, A=B, A<B.

levelsV2.name: Simple ALU (Add/Sub)
levelsV2.description: 4-bit ALU with add/subtract operations. Op=0: add, Op=1: subtract.

levelsV2.name: Complete 4-bit ALU
levelsV2.description: Full ALU with 4 operations: AND, OR, ADD, SUB. 2-bit operation select.

levelsV2.name: 4-bit Counter
levelsV2.description: Count from 0 to 15 and repeat. Use clock input.

chapters.chapterDescription: Bridge the gap between simple logic gates and real-world computing! Learn to work with 8-bit data buses - the fundamental unit of computer memory. Master parallel processing, understand carry propagation across bytes, and build circuits that manipulate data the way real processors do. From simple operations to a complete 8-bit ALU, you'll discover how computers process information at the byte level.

levelsV2.name: 8-Bit Wire
levelsV2.description: Connect the 8-bit input directly to the 8-bit output. This introduces the concept of multi-bit buses - bundles of wires that carry parallel data signals. Think of it as moving an entire byte of information at once!

levelsV2.name: 8-Bit 2-to-1 Multiplexer
levelsV2.description: Build an 8-bit 2-to-1 multiplexer. When SEL=0, output A; when SEL=1, output B. This circuit selects between two 8-bit data sources based on a single control signal.

levelsV2.name: 8-Bit Adder
levelsV2.description: Add two 8-bit numbers with carry-in and carry-out. This is real binary arithmetic! The carry ripples through all 8 bits, just like carrying in decimal addition.

levelsV2.name: 8-Bit Equality Comparator
levelsV2.description: Compare two 8-bit numbers for equality. Output 1 if A equals B, 0 otherwise. All 8 bits must match! This is how computers check if two values are the same.

levelsV2.name: 8-Bit Greater Than
levelsV2.description: Compare two 8-bit unsigned numbers. Output 1 if A > B, 0 otherwise. Start comparing from the most significant bit (MSB) - just like comparing decimal numbers from left to right!

levelsV2.name: 8-Bit Left Shifter
levelsV2.description: Shift all bits left by 1 position. Bit 7 receives bit 6, bit 6 receives bit 5, and so on. Bit 0 becomes 0. Fun fact: shifting left by 1 is the same as multiplying by 2!

levelsV2.name: 8-Bit Incrementer
levelsV2.description: Add 1 to the 8-bit input. This is a special case of addition used everywhere in computers - incrementing program counters, array indices, loop counters, etc.

levelsV2.name: 8-Bit ALU
levelsV2.description: Build an 8-bit Arithmetic Logic Unit with 4 operations selected by 2 control bits (OP-0, OP-1): 00=bitwise-AND, 01=bitwise-OR, 10=ADD, 11=SUB. Combine everything you've learned into a real data processing unit!
